page_review.title: Low-Poly PSX Style Industrial Metal Doors Pack
page_review.author: Icevanilla
page_review.description: A pack of 6 low-poly PSX-style industrial metal doors for utility, service and industrial environments, with clean, worn, rusty, reinforced and heavy variants.
page_review.download_modal_terms: Author must be credited. Commercial use is allowed.
page_review.visible_geometry: A row of industrial metal door variants including plain, windowed, worn and heavy leaves; the modeled Metal_Door_007 pair forms a double-leaf display and is excluded.
page_review.author_dependency_comment: The author says the model uses one texture atlas included with the FBX; local USDZ contains one atlas.

selected_source.frame_reuse_review: The 001 leaf has no source frame. Reuse the original Metal_Doorframe_002 mesh from the same CC BY pack; its 003 leaf and the 001 leaf share the same 0.8713 x 1.8822 x 0.1034 m envelope. Translate the frame rigidly by the measured source-display offset so its modeled aperture surrounds the 001 leaf. Do not alter either mesh, UV or map.
selected_source.operation: Compose this single leaf with an existing size-matched frame from the same pack, rigidly relocated. This is an explicit simulation assembly; preserve original geometry, UVs, texture and downloaded USDZ. Exclude the double leaf and other displays.

license_dependency_review: One 1024 x 256 base-color atlas is packaged in the CC BY USDZ; stage metadata matches the page author, CC-BY-4.0 and source URL. No separate texture terms were found.
local_geometry_review: Original slab and modeled frame remain separately collidable in a reviewed surface-mounted simulation assembly; source geometry and atlas are retained. Attempt 000008: reviewed surface-mounted closed-unlatched assembly passes static and one RTX 4090 run to 91.0 degrees. All frame/slab/handle collisions and physics tolerances are retained; the 2% moving-fit bound is unchanged. Robot/expert qualification remains pending.

clearance_measurement.interpretation: The 3.262% minimum applies only to fitting the slab inside this opening. The final surface mount instead preserves overlap against the jamb face; no extension of the 2% shrink allowance is required.
